q: What is leadership?
r: The ability to influence and guide others toward a shared goal
Leaders inspire people to act.
w: The authority to give orders without explaining
The ownership of a company's shares
The skill of working alone on every task

q: What is the difference between a leader and a manager?
r: Leaders inspire and set direction; managers organize and control tasks
Both roles are valuable.
w: Leaders only follow orders; managers never do
The roles are not defined that way.
Managers inspire; leaders only count money
There is no difference between them

q: What is an autocratic leadership style?
r: The leader makes decisions alone with little input from the team
It can be fast but may lower morale.
w: The leader shares decisions equally with the team
The leader lets the team decide everything

q: What is a democratic (participative) leadership style?
r: The leader invites team input before making decisions
It builds buy-in and ownership.

q: What is a laissez-faire leadership style?
r: The leader gives the team wide freedom with little direction
It works with skilled, motivated teams.
w: The leader votes on every choice
The leader takes all decisions alone

q: What is transformational leadership?
r: Inspiring followers to look beyond self-interest and achieve a shared vision
The leader motivates change.
w: Rewarding and punishing based on performance only
Letting followers do whatever they like
Leading only in times of crisis

q: What is transactional leadership?
r: Using rewards and penalties to motivate performance against clear goals
It relies on exchange.
w: Inspiring people through a shared vision
Serving the needs of followers first

q: What is servant leadership?
r: Putting the needs of followers first to help them grow and succeed
The leader serves the team.
w: Making followers serve the leader's wishes

q: A team is highly skilled and self-motivated and needs little supervision. Which style is likely to work well?
r: Laissez-faire or delegating style
Skilled teams thrive with freedom.
w: Strict autocratic control of every task
Silence and no support at all

q: A new team with little experience faces an emergency. Which style may be most effective?
r: A directive style that gives clear instructions
Inexperienced teams need clear guidance in crisis.
w: A hands-off style with no direction
A style that waits for everyone to vote
It wastes time in an emergency.
A style that ignores the problem

q: What is situational leadership?
r: Adapting leadership style to the readiness of followers and the situation
No single style works best everywhere.
w: Using the same style in every case
Letting followers choose the leader each day
Leading only from a fixed location

q: Which trait is most associated with effective leaders?
r: Integrity
Trust is the foundation of leadership.

q: What is emotional intelligence?
r: The ability to recognize and manage your own emotions and those of others
It supports teamwork and leadership.
w: The ability to memorize large amounts of data
The ability to avoid feelings entirely
The ability to speak several languages

q: What is empathy?
r: Understanding and sharing the feelings of another person
It helps leaders connect with teams.

q: What is active listening?
r: Fully concentrating on a speaker, then responding thoughtfully
It includes paraphrasing and asking questions.
w: Waiting for your turn to talk
Checking your phone while someone speaks

q: What is constructive feedback?
r: Specific, respectful input meant to help someone improve
It focuses on behavior, not personality.
w: Harsh criticism of a person's character

q: Which statement is the best example of constructive feedback?
r: Your report was clear, but adding data on costs would strengthen it
It is specific and offers a path forward.

q: What is a vision in leadership?
r: A clear picture of a desirable future that inspires people
Leaders communicate it to align effort.
w: A prediction of next week's weather
A list of this month's expenses

q: Why is communicating a vision important?
r: It aligns people around common goals and motivates action
Shared direction improves teamwork.
w: It keeps the vision secret from the team

q: What is motivation?
r: The internal or external drive that causes a person to act toward a goal
Leaders influence motivation.
w: The result of a performance review
The hours worked in a week

q: According to Maslow's hierarchy of needs, which need comes first?
r: Physiological needs such as food and shelter
Basic needs must be met first.

q: Which is the correct order of Maslow's hierarchy from bottom to top?
r: Physiological, safety, belonging, esteem, self-actualization
This is the standard order.

q: According to Herzberg's two-factor theory, which is a hygiene factor?
r: Salary and working conditions
Hygiene factors prevent dissatisfaction.

q: According to Herzberg's theory, which is a motivator?
r: Recognition and opportunities for advancement
Motivators create satisfaction.

q: What is intrinsic motivation?
r: Motivation that comes from inside, such as enjoyment or pride in the work
It is driven by personal satisfaction.
w: Motivation that comes from rewards given by others
Motivation that comes from fear only
Motivation that comes from lack of choices

q: What is extrinsic motivation?
r: Motivation that comes from outside rewards such as pay or praise
The reward is separate from the task.
w: Motivation that comes from personal interest

q: A student volunteers at a shelter because it feels meaningful. This is an example of:
r: Intrinsic motivation
The reward is inner satisfaction.

q: What is a role model?
r: A person whose behavior others admire and copy
Leaders act as role models.
w: A person who only gives orders
That is not a role model.

q: What does it mean to lead by example?
r: Showing the behavior and standards you expect from others
Actions speak louder than words.
w: Telling others to do what you will not do

q: What is accountability in leadership?
r: Taking responsibility for decisions and their results
Leaders own both successes and failures.

q: What is trust in a team?
r: Confidence that members will act honestly and reliably
Trust helps teams perform.
w: Belief that no one will ever disagree

q: A leader promises to approve vacation requests but later refuses without explanation. What is the likely effect?
r: Trust in the leader declines
Broken promises erode trust.

q: What is conflict resolution?
r: Finding a solution that settles a disagreement fairly
Good leaders address conflict early.
w: Ignoring a disagreement until it ends
That does not resolve the cause.

q: What is a win-win solution?
r: An outcome that benefits all parties in a disagreement
It requires cooperation.
w: An outcome where one side wins and the other loses
An outcome where both sides lose

q: Two team members disagree about how to split a task. What is the best first step for a leader?
r: Listen to both sides and help them find a shared solution
Understanding comes before deciding.
w: Choose a side immediately without listening
That does not solve the issue.

q: What is mentoring?
r: A relationship in which an experienced person guides a less experienced one
Mentors share advice and encouragement.
w: A test given to new hires
A job title for a manager

q: What is coaching?
r: Helping someone improve specific skills through guidance and feedback
It is focused on development.

q: What is a stakeholder in a leadership context?
r: Anyone who is affected by or has an interest in a decision
Leaders weigh stakeholder views.
w: Only the person who makes the decision
A stake used to mark property

q: What is ethical leadership?
r: Leading in ways that are honest, fair and respect others
Ethical leaders set a standard.
w: Leading by whatever brings the fastest profit

q: A leader discovers that a team member padded expense reports. The ethical response is to:
r: Address the issue through proper policy, fairly and consistently
Consistency and fairness matter.
w: Ignore it because the amount is small

q: What does it mean to be adaptable as a leader?
r: Adjusting approach when conditions or needs change
Flexibility helps teams succeed.
w: Refusing to change plans no matter what
Changing mind every minute without reason

q: What is a common mistake of new leaders?
r: Trying to do everything themselves instead of delegating
Overload hurts the team.

q: What is peer pressure?
r: Influence from people of the same group to act in a certain way
It can be positive or negative.
w: A rule written in a handbook

q: What is a parliamentary procedure used for?
r: Running meetings in an orderly and fair way
Robert's Rules of Order is a common guide.

q: In parliamentary procedure, what is a motion?
r: A formal proposal that a group take action
Members offer motions during meetings.
w: A physical movement by a member

q: In parliamentary procedure, what must happen after a motion is made?
r: It needs a second before discussion
Seconding shows another member supports discussion.

q: What are meeting minutes?
r: The official written record of what happened in a meeting
They list decisions and actions.
w: The length of time a meeting lasts

q: What is an agenda?
r: A list of topics to be covered in a meeting
It keeps the meeting focused.
w: A record of past meeting decisions
A list of rules for employees

q: Which practice makes a meeting more productive?
r: Sharing an agenda in advance and keeping to time
Preparation keeps focus.

q: What is public speaking confidence built through?
r: Practice and preparation
Rehearsal reduces anxiety.
w: Reading from a script word for word at all times

q: Which is the best way to organize a speech?
r: Introduction, body and conclusion
A clear structure helps listeners.

q: What is nonverbal communication?
r: Messages sent through body language, facial expression and tone
It often reveals feelings.
w: Messages sent in written form only

q: A speaker says 'I'm happy to be here' while looking at the floor with crossed arms. What message may the audience receive?
r: Mixed signals, because body language does not match the words
Nonverbal cues can contradict speech.
w: The body language suggests the opposite.
